title: Evidence measurement artifact
description: The wire shape a lane or an oracle emits. Contract 2.1.0 adds this as the fourth sealed bundle member: the contract describes these fields in prose, and prose is not a shape two independent authors can emit compatibly. Nothing here is corpus-derived — a schema is protocol under contract 1.2, and says nothing about what the corpus contains.

role.description: Contract 4.4. A run has at most one oracle; without one it has no correctness verdict.

identity.title: Physical occurrence identity
identity.description: Contract 3.2 — (path, blob, start_byte, end_byte). Profile is NOT part of the key; it is carried on an occurrence for membership (contract 2.1) and is optional on a role binding, where it decides nothing.

field_value.description: Contract 6 — a field is in exactly one state. `value` is absent when the state is not `present`.

literal.description: Contract 3.5 — must equal the UTF-8 decoding of the span. The comparator checks it against the blob; the schema can only require that it is present.

fields.description: Contract 3.3 — the registry's declared fields, compared. Keyed by field name.

quoted_context.description: Contract 3.6 — a rebaseline aid, resolved to a span and never guessed at. Decides no verdict.

anchor.description: Contract 4.3 — exactly one row per in-scope anchor, and the disposition must be consistent with the roles it names. The schema fixes the shape; the comparator checks the consistency, which a schema cannot express.

roles.description: Role name to the identity filling it. An UNFILLED ROLE IS ABSENT, never null: contract 4.3 makes which roles are filled part of the disposition's meaning, and two wire spellings of one fact are two things for a lane to differ about. Only filled roles appear.

qualifiers.description: Contract 7.5 — annotates a row, never replaces its status.

provenance.description: Contract 4.4 property 2 — how this row was adjudicated. An oracle records it per row.

policy.description: Contract 4.5 — structured and digested, never a bare name. `class` is deliberately free text: contract 4.2 removed the fixed vocabulary, and an enum here would restore it.

parameters.description: Flat: every value is a scalar. Contract 4.5 fixes it flat so two declarations are comparable key by key.

attestation.description: Contract 11.4 — a claim by its lane, not a proof. What a comparator can decide is that it exists and agrees with the artifact beside it.

prohibited_inputs_accessed.description: Empty is a claim; absent is a silence. Contract 11.4 requires it written either way.
